# Fab accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

| Result                | Count |
| :-------------------- | :---- |
| ✅ Supports           | 21    |
| ⚠️ Partially Supports | 4     |
| ❌ Does Not Support   | 0     |
| ➖ Not Applicable     | 30    |
| 🚩 Flagged            | 6/25  |

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum).** <!-- 1.4.3:gap:start -->Extended labels in `info` (`3.86:1`) and `warning` (`3.11:1`) are less than `4.5:1`. On keyboard focus, the focus ripple behind the label lowers each palette color to `2.23:1` (`warning`) to `3.57:1` (`secondary`), and `primary` to `2.80:1`. A press lowers them to `4.16:1` or less. Use `disableFocusRipple` with the `focusVisible` theme ring.<!-- 1.4.3:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.10 Reflow.** <!-- 1.4.10:gap:start -->The extended Fab has a fixed height. At 320 CSS px, a label that wraps is taller than the Fab and spills out of it.<!-- 1.4.10:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.** <!-- 1.4.11:gap:start -->The default focus indicator is the focus ripple, at `1.39:1` to `1.85:1` against the fill. On the ripple, `primary`, `info`, `success`, and `warning` icons are less than `3:1`. The `focusVisible` theme ring does not remove the ripple, so also set `disableFocusRipple`.<!-- 1.4.11:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.12 Text Spacing.** <!-- 1.4.12:gap:start -->The extended Fab has a fixed height. The WCAG letter and word spacing can make a one-line label wrap. Two lines are taller than the `medium` and `small` Fabs, so the label spills out.<!-- 1.4.12:gap:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.2:start -->

- The Fab is one control. An extended Fab renders its children in source order, usually the icon and then the label. The icon is `aria-hidden`.
- The author often gives the Fab a fixed position, so it can show far from its place in the DOM. Its place in the reading order is an author decision.

**Manual testing steps**

1. On a page with a fixed Fab, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> repeatedly.
2. Write down when the Fab gets focus.
3. Compare this with the place where the Fab shows on the page.

<!-- 1.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.2:pass:start -->the Fab gets focus at a logical point, for example after the main content that it acts on.<!-- 1.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.3:start -->

- Users identify a Fab by its accessible name, not only by its shape, color, or position.
- Do not refer to the Fab by shape or position alone in instructions. For example, do not write "press the round button at the bottom right".

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find product copy that tells users to operate the Fab.
2. Make sure that it names the action, not only the shape, color, or position of the Fab.

<!-- 1.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.3:pass:start -->each instruction names the action, for example "select Compose".<!-- 1.3.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.5 Images of Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.4.5:start -->

- The Fab renders an SVG icon, an icon-font glyph, or real text. None of these is an image of text.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Inspect each Fab in the product.
2. Make sure that no icon is an image of words.

<!-- 1.4.5:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.5:pass:start -->no Fab shows words as an image. A logo with an accessible name is an exception.<!-- 1.4.5:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 2.4.11:start -->

- The author often sets `position: fixed` on a Fab. The component sets `z-index: theme.zIndex.fab` (1050). So the Fab can hide other focused elements, which is the main risk for this criterion.
- When you press <kbd>Tab</kbd> forward, the browser scrolls each element to the bottom edge, which is under the Fab. Set `scroll-padding-bottom` on the scroll container to at least the Fab height plus its offset.
- The Fab itself can also be hidden by a sticky footer or a banner.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Put the Fab in a fixed position at the bottom of a long page.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> forward through the content behind the Fab.
3. At each focused element near the Fab, look for the focus indicator.
4. Make the browser window short and do the test again.

<!-- 2.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.11:pass:start -->the Fab never fully hides a focused element.<!-- 2.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 3.2.4 Consistent Identification · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 3.2.4:start -->

- The component gives one stable accessible name for each set of props.
- Consistency is a property across pages. The same Fab action must use the same icon and label on each page.

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the Fabs that do the same job across the product.
2. Compare their icons and labels.

<!-- 3.2.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.2.4:pass:start -->the same job uses the same icon and label, and no icon is used for different jobs.<!-- 3.2.4:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.1.1 Non-text Content · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `Fab.test.js`

<!-- 1.1.1:start -->

- An icon-only Fab has no visible text. Its accessible name comes from `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, a `Tooltip` title, or `titleAccess` on the icon. The author must supply it, and the component does not warn when it is missing.
- An extended Fab takes its name from its visible label.
- `SvgIcon` and `Icon` children are `aria-hidden`, unless `SvgIcon` sets `titleAccess`. The author must hide an icon of another type.
- A unit test confirms that `aria-label` names the Fab and that the icon is hidden. axe-core `button-name` confirms that each demo has a name, and `aria-command-name` confirms the non-native fixture. Both rules are listed under 4.1.2.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari).
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an icon-only Fab and to an extended Fab.
3. Listen to the announcement for each.

<!-- 1.1.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.1.1:pass:start -->the icon-only Fab announces its `aria-label`, the extended Fab announces its visible text, and the icon is silent.<!-- 1.1.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- The component sets the correct role: `button`, `link` with `href`, or `role="button"` for a non-native element. It sets the disabled state. axe-core ARIA rules pass on the demos.
- A toggle Fab, such as "Add to favorites", needs `aria-pressed` from the author.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader.
2. Move the screen-reader cursor to a plain Fab, an `href` Fab, a disabled one, and one with `aria-pressed`.
3. Listen to the role and state for each.

In NVDA, move the cursor with the arrow keys. In VoiceOver, use <kbd>VO</kbd>+<kbd>Right Arrow</kbd>.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->the screen reader announces "button", "link", the disabled state, and the pressed state where they apply.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.1 Use of Color · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.4.1:start -->

- The purpose of a Fab comes from its icon and its label. Focus and disabled do not rely on color alone.
- The `color` prop only changes the fill. If two Fabs differ only by color, the meaning is lost without color.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In Chrome DevTools, open the Rendering tab.
2. Select Emulate vision deficiencies > Achromatopsia.
3. Make sure that you can identify the purpose of each Fab.

<!-- 1.4.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.1:pass:start -->the purpose of each Fab stays clear without color.<!-- 1.4.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) · AA

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Fab.test.js` · axe-core `color-contrast` ❌

<!-- 1.4.3:start -->

- An extended Fab renders `contrastText` on `main`, like a contained Button. `info` (`3.86:1`) and `warning` (`3.11:1`) are less than `4.5:1`. A unit test confirms that only these colors fail, from the [palette contrast contract](../../test/contrastContract.ts). axe-core `color-contrast` records the failure.
- On hover, the fill changes to `dark`. Each color then reaches `4.5:1`, except `warning` at `3.79:1`.
- On keyboard focus and on press, the ripple paints `contrastText` at `30%` over the label. Each palette color is then less than `4.5:1`: `2.23:1` (`warning`) to `3.57:1` (`secondary`) on focus, and up to `4.16:1` on a mouse press. This also applies to a contained Button.
- The `focusVisible` theme ring does not remove the focus ripple. To keep the label on the plain fill, set `disableFocusRipple` with the ring.
- The `default` color is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.87)` on `grey[300]`, at `12.77:1` (`grey[900]`, `12.20:1`, with CSS theme variables). It stays at `7.43:1` or more on the ripple.
- With `color="inherit"`, the label takes the parent text color on a `grey[300]` fill. The author must check this pair. Disabled Fabs are exempt.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker, measure the label against the fill, for each color in use.
2. Hover over each Fab and measure again.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to each Fab and measure the label on the focus ripple.
4. Measure the icon against `3:1`, see 1.4.11.

<!-- 1.4.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.3:pass:start -->the label is at least `4.5:1` in the resting, hover, focused, and pressed states. `info` and `warning` fail at rest, and each palette color fails on the ripple.<!-- 1.4.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- A circular Fab has a fixed size of 40 to 56 CSS px. An extended Fab is as wide as its label. A Playwright test confirms that the extended-size demo does not scroll horizontally at 320 px.
- At 320 px, a label wider than the viewport wraps. Two lines at line-height 1.75 are 49 px high. The fixed height does not grow, so the label spills out of the Fab, as under text-only resize in 1.4.4.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Set the viewport width to 320 CSS px.
2. Render an extended Fab with a label that wraps.
3. Make sure that the full label stays inside the Fab.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.10:pass:start -->the full label stays inside the Fab. A label that wraps fails with the default styles.<!-- 1.4.10:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `Fab.test.js`

<!-- 1.4.11:start -->

- The icon is `contrastText` on `main`. A unit test confirms that it reaches `3:1` against the fill at rest, in each of the six palette colors (`primary` to `warning`). `warning` is the lowest, at `3.11:1`.
- The focus indicator is the focus ripple: `contrastText` at `30%` opacity over the fill. It is `1.39:1` (`warning`) to `1.85:1` (`default`) against the fill, which is less than `3:1`. The box-shadow does not change on focus.
- On the ripple, the icon is less than `3:1` in `warning` (`2.23:1`), `info` (`2.54:1`), `primary` (`2.80:1`), and `success` (`2.92:1`).
- The `focusVisible` theme ring does not remove the focus ripple. Set `disableFocusRipple` with the ring, so that the icon stays on the plain fill.
- The `default` fill (`grey[300]`) is `1.32:1` against a white page. The icon or label identifies the Fab, so the fill boundary does not need `3:1`.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker, measure the icon against the fill, for each color in use.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the Fab so that the focus indicator shows.
3. Sample the rendered ripple color with the DevTools color picker.
4. Measure the ripple against the fill, and the icon against the ripple.
5. Set the `focusVisible` theme ring and `disableFocusRipple`.
6. Measure the ring against the page behind the Fab.

<!-- 1.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.11:pass:start -->the icon and the focus indicator are at least `3:1`. Disabled Fabs are exempt. The default focus ripple fails. The `focusVisible` theme ring with `disableFocusRipple` fixes it on a light page. On a colored or dark page, measure the ring.<!-- 1.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.12 Text Spacing · AA

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.12:start -->

- A Playwright test applies the WCAG text-spacing values to the extended-size demo. Its short labels do not overflow.
- The label already has line-height 1.75, so the WCAG value of 1.5 does not make it taller.
- The letter and word spacing make the label wider, so a one-line label can wrap. Two lines are 42 px high at line-height 1.5, and 49 px at 1.75. This is more than the `medium` (40 px) and `small` (34 px) heights, so the text spills out of the Fab.
- The second column of the `FabA11yLongLabel` fixture shows this. Each label fits on one line at the default spacing, and wraps to two lines with the WCAG values.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Render a `small` extended Fab whose label fits on one line, in a container a little wider than the Fab.
2. Apply the WCAG text-spacing values, for example with a text-spacing bookmarklet.
3. Make sure that the full label stays inside the Fab.

<!-- 1.4.12:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.12:pass:start -->the full label stays inside the Fab. A label that wraps to two lines fails in the `medium` and `small` sizes with the default styles.<!-- 1.4.12:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `link-name` ✅

<!-- 2.4.4:start -->

- This applies only with `href`, where the root is an `<a>`. axe-core `link-name` confirms that the link fixture has a name.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find Fabs that use `href`.
2. Read the name of each, together with the content around it.

<!-- 2.4.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.4:pass:start -->a user can tell where each link goes.<!-- 2.4.4:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.4.6:start -->

- The accessible name is the label of the control. axe-core `button-name` and `link-name` confirm that it is present.
- Whether the label describes the action is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the name of each Fab.
2. Read each name without its icon.

<!-- 2.4.6:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.6:pass:start -->each name tells the action, for example "Compose message", not "Add icon".<!-- 2.4.6:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.7 Focus Visible · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 2.4.7:start -->

- Keyboard focus shows the focus ripple. A mouse click does not show it. A Playwright test confirms that keyboard focus changes how the Fab looks.
- On focus, the box-shadow stays at `shadows[6]`, the same as at rest. `disableRipple` and `disableFocusRipple` remove the ripple, and then the Fab has no focus indicator.
- With `focusVisible: true` on the theme, keyboard focus adds an outline ring next to the shadow. See [Focus visible](https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/focus-visible/). A Playwright test confirms the ring with the ripple disabled.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a Fab.
2. Make sure that a focus indicator shows.
3. Click a Fab with the mouse.
4. Make sure that the focus indicator does not show.
5. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a Fab with `disableRipple` and the default theme.
6. Set `focusVisible: true` on the theme, and press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the same Fab.

<!-- 2.4.7:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.7:pass:start -->each Fab shows a visible indicator on keyboard focus. With `disableRipple` and the default theme, no indicator shows, and the author must add one. The `focusVisible` theme ring fixes it.<!-- 2.4.7:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `Fab.test.js` · axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` ✅, `aria-command-name` ✅, `aria-conditional-attr` ✅, `aria-deprecated-role` ✅, `aria-hidden-focus` ✅, `aria-prohibited-attr` ✅, `aria-required-attr` ✅, `aria-roles` ✅, `aria-valid-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr-value` ✅, `button-name` ✅, `link-name` ✅, `nested-interactive` ✅

<!-- 4.1.2:start -->

- A native `<button>`, an `<a>` with `href`, and `role="button"` on a non-native element each set the correct role. `disabled` sets the state. Unit tests and the axe-core `aria-*` rules, `button-name`, and `nested-interactive` confirm this.
- The author supplies the name of an icon-only Fab with `aria-label`, and the pressed state with `aria-pressed`.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a native Fab, an `href` Fab, and a non-native one.
3. Move the screen-reader cursor to the disabled Fab, which is not in the tab order.
4. Listen to the name, role, and state for each.

In NVDA, move the cursor with the arrow keys. In VoiceOver, use <kbd>VO</kbd>+<kbd>Right Arrow</kbd>.

<!-- 4.1.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.2:pass:start -->the name, role, and state are correct for each kind. The disabled one announces "disabled", and the `href` one "link".<!-- 4.1.2:pass:end -->

### ⚙️ Automated

#### 1.4.4 Resize Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.4:start -->

- The label and the icon use `rem`, and the extended Fab has a fixed px height (48, 40, or 34 px). Under 200% page zoom, the height and the label scale together, so the label stays inside the Fab. Page zoom decides the 1.4.4 rating (WCAG technique G142). A Playwright test confirms this on the extended-size demo.
- Under text-only resize, the label grows but the height does not. A label that wraps then grows taller than the Fab, and the spilled `contrastText` can be invisible on the page. The third column of the `FabA11yLongLabel` fixture shows this: it doubles the rem sizes, and each label wraps to two or three lines of 49 px. Three lines are 147 px high, so they spill about 50 px above and below the 48 px Fab.
- A second Playwright test confirms that the extended-size demo, with short labels, survives a 200% text-only resize.
- To make long labels safe under text-only resize, set `height: 'auto'`, `minHeight: 48`, and vertical padding with `sx`. Then the Fab grows with its label.

<!-- 1.4.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.4:pass:start -->the full label stays readable inside the Fab at 200% page zoom.<!-- 1.4.4:pass:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A).** <!-- 2.2.2:start -->The focus ripple pulses while the Fab has keyboard focus. The user starts it by moving focus, so it does not start automatically.<!-- 2.2.2:end -->
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** Activates on a simple click; reads no device motion.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A).** <!-- 3.3.2:start -->A Fab asks for no input.<!-- 3.3.2:end -->
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.
- **4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).** Emits no status messages; state changes are covered by 4.1.2.

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

- **2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), 44 px.** `large` (56 px) and `medium` (48 px) circular Fabs are larger than 44 px. A `small` Fab (40 px) and the `small` and `medium` extended Fabs (34 and 40 px high) are smaller. `🚩`
- **2.4.13 Focus Appearance.** The focus ripple does not meet it, because its contrast against the fill is `1.39:1` to `1.85:1`, less than `3:1`. `🚩`
- **1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced), 7:1.** Each palette color is less than 7:1 with `contrastText`. Only `default` passes. `🚩`
- **2.3.3 Animation from Interactions.** The ripple honors `prefers-reduced-motion` when the theme sets `motion.reducedMotion`. The default is `never`. `disableRipple` also removes it. `🚩`

<!-- level-aaa:end -->

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
- **Component version.** `@mui/material` 10.0.0-alpha.0.

<!-- scope:start -->

- **Scope.** The Fab component in isolation, rendered through its documented API, in the circular and extended variants.
- **Automated.** axe-core in the Playwright test harness, on the Fab demos and fixtures in [`floating-action-button.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/floating-action-button/floating-action-button.a11y.json). Interaction and contrast tests are in `Fab.test.js` and `ButtonBase.test.js`.
